1976년 7월 20일 화성에 내려 처음으로 표면 사진을 보내고, 6년: It landed on Mars on July 20, 1976, sent the first photographs from the surface, and worked for over six years.
타이탄(남위 10.6도, 서경 192.3도) 150km 안에 내려앉기: Land within 150 km of the place on Titan (10.6° S, 192.3° W)
2005년 1월 14일 타이탄에 내렸습니다. 지구에서 가장 먼 곳에 내린: It landed on Titan on January 14, 2005: the farthest landing from Earth.
토성의 구름 꼭대기에 닿기: Touch the tops of Saturn's clouds
13년 동안 토성을 돈 카시니는 2017년 9월 15일 토성 대기로 뛰어: After 13 years round Saturn, Cassini plunged into Saturn's air and burned up on September 15, 2017.
명왕성 표면 12,500km 안을 지나기: Pass within 12,500 km of Pluto's surface
2015년 7월 14일, 9년 반을 날아온 뉴허라이즌스가 명왕성을 12,: On July 14, 2015, after flying nine and a half years, New Horizons swept past Pluto at 12,500 km.
핼리 혜성의 핵 600km 안을 지나기: Pass within 600 km of the core of Halley's Comet
1986년 3월 14일 지오토가 핼리의 핵을 596km 거리에서 지나며: On March 14, 1986, Giotto passed Halley's core at 596 km and took the first clear pictures of a comet's core.
1977년 떠난 보이저 1호는 2012년 8월 태양권을 벗어나 별 사이: Voyager 1 left in 1977 and in August 2012 left the Sun's bubble for the space between the stars.
지구에서 6,000만km 넘게 멀어지기 (실제 거리로 60억km, 명왕성: Go more than 60 million km from Earth (6 billion km in real distance, about Pluto's orbit)
1990년 2월 14일 보이저 1호가 60억km 밖에서 돌아본 지구는 한: On February 14, 1990, Voyager 1 looked back from 6 billion km: Earth was a blue dot less than a pixel wide.
지구 동해의 독도(북위 37.2도, 동경 131.9도) 40km 안에 내: Land within 40 km of Dokdo in the East Sea on Earth (37.2° N, 131.9° E)
대한민국의 가장 동쪽 섬입니다. 울릉도에서 87.4km 떨어져 있고, 동: The easternmost island of Korea. It lies 87.4 km from Ulleungdo and is made of an east island, a west island and 89 rocks.
비의 바다 동쪽: east of the Sea of Rains
1959년 9월 14일 소련의 루나 2호가 이곳에 부딪혔습니다. 사람이: On September 14, 1959, the Soviet Luna 2 struck here: the first thing people made to touch another world.
폭풍의 대양 서쪽: west of the Ocean of Storms
1966년 2월 3일 처음으로 달에 부드럽게 내려 표면 사진을 보냈습니다: On February 3, 1966, it made the first soft landing on the Moon and sent photographs of the surface. It showed the Moon is not a swamp of dust.
1966년 6월 미국이 처음으로 달에 부드럽게 내린 착륙선입니다. 사진: In June 1966, the first American lander to set down softly on the Moon. It sent 11,000 photographs.
1968년 1월 서베이어의 마지막 착륙선이 티코 분화구 가장자리에 내려: In January 1968 the last Surveyor landed by the rim of Tycho and tested the soil of the highlands.
1969년 11월, 2년 반 전에 내린 서베이어 3호 곁 160m쯤에 내: In November 1969 it landed about 160 m from Surveyor 3, which had landed two and a half years before, and brought parts of it back to Earth.
1970년 9월 사람 없이 달의 흙 101g을 떠서 지구로 가져온 첫 탐: In September 1970, the first probe to scoop up Moon soil (101 g) and bring it to Earth with nobody aboard.
1970년 11월 루나 17호가 내려놓은 첫 달 탐사차입니다. 바퀴 여덟: The first Moon rover, set down by Luna 17 in November 1970. On eight wheels it drove 10.5 km in ten months.
1971년 2월 앨런 셰퍼드가 이곳에서 골프공 두 개를 쳤습니다. 손수레: In February 1971 Alan Shepard hit two golf balls here. Pulling a handcart, they gathered 43 kg of rock.
1971년 7월 처음으로 월면차를 몰았습니다. 깃털과 망치를 함께 떨어뜨: In July 1971 a Moon car was driven for the first time. A feather and a hammer were dropped together and landed together.
1972년 4월 달의 고지대에 내린 하나뿐인 아폴로입니다. 월면차로 27: In April 1972, the only Apollo to land in the Moon's highlands. The Moon car drove 27 km.
1972년 12월 사람이 마지막으로 달을 걸은 곳입니다. 지질학자 슈미트: In December 1972, the last place people walked on the Moon. The geologist Schmitt found orange soil.
1973년 1월 루나 21호가 내려놓은 탐사차입니다. 넉 달 동안 39k: The rover set down by Luna 21 in January 1973. It drove 39 km in four months, a record that stood for over 40 years.
In August 1976, the last Soviet Moon probe brought back 170 g of soil. For 37 years after it nobody landed on the Moon.
비의 바다 북쪽: north of the Sea of Rains
2013년 12월 중국의 창어 3호가 탐사차 위투(옥토끼)와 함께 내렸습: In December 2013 China's Chang'e 3 landed with the rover Yutu (Jade Rabbit): the first Moon landing in 37 years.
뒷면 폰 카르만 분화구: Von Kármán Crater on the far side
2019년 1월 3일 처음으로 달의 뒷면에 내렸습니다. 탐사차 위투 2호: On January 3, 2019, the first landing on the far side of the Moon. The rover Yutu 2 went with it.
폭풍의 대양 북쪽: north of the Ocean of Storms
2020년 12월 달 흙 1,731g을 지구로 가져왔습니다. 44년 만의: In December 2020 it brought 1,731 g of Moon soil to Earth: the first Moon samples in 44 years.
2023년 8월 23일 인도의 비크람 착륙선이 달 남극 가까이에 처음 내: On August 23, 2023, India's lander Vikram made the first landing near the Moon's south pole. The rover Pragyan went with it.
2024년 1월 일본의 슬림이 목표 100m 안에 내렸습니다. 엔진 하나: In January 2024 Japan's SLIM landed within 100 m of its target. One engine had fallen off, and it came to rest on its nose.
남극 말라퍼트 A 분화구: Malapert A Crater at the south pole
2024년 2월 민간 기업이 만든 착륙선이 처음으로 달에 내렸습니다. 다: In February 2024 a lander built by a private company landed on the Moon for the first time. A leg caught and it lay on its side.
뒷면 아폴로 분지: the Apollo basin on the far side
2024년 6월 달 뒷면의 흙 1,935g을 처음으로 지구에 가져왔습니다: In June 2024 it brought 1,935 g of soil from the Moon's far side to Earth, for the first time.
2025년 3월 2일 민간 착륙선으로는 처음 똑바로 서서 내려, 2주 동: On March 2, 2025, it was the first private lander to set down upright. It worked for two weeks and photographed a sunset on the Moon.
1971년 12월 2일 소련의 마스 3호가 화성에 처음 부드럽게 내렸습니: On December 2, 1971, the Soviet Mars 3 made the first soft landing on Mars. Its signal stopped in under 20 seconds.
It landed on September 3, 1976, and photographed frost on the ground each morning. It worked 3 years 7 months.
1997년 7월 4일 공기 주머니에 싸여 튀며 내렸습니다. 첫 화성 탐사: On July 4, 1997, it landed bouncing inside airbags. Sojourner, the first Mars rover, roamed for 83 days.
2003년 성탄절에 내린 영국 착륙선입니다. 소식이 끊겼다가 11년 뒤: A British lander that came down on Christmas Day 2003. Nothing was heard of it; eleven years later a photograph showed it with its solar panels half open.
2004년 1월 내린 탐사차입니다. 90일 임무였으나 6년을 일하다 모래: A rover that landed in January 2004. Sent for 90 days, it worked six years until it stuck in sand.
90일 임무로 왔다가 14년 동안 45km를 달렸습니다. 2018년 먼지: Sent for 90 days, it drove 45 km in 14 years. Contact was lost in a dust storm in 2018.
2008년 5월 화성 북극 가까이 내려 흙 밑의 얼음을 파냈습니다. 겨울: In May 2008 it landed near Mars's north pole and dug up the ice under the soil. When winter came it froze and stopped.
2012년 8월 자동차만 한 탐사차가 줄에 매달려 내렸습니다. 지금도 샤: In August 2012 a rover the size of a car was lowered on cables. It is still climbing Mount Sharp.
It landed in November 2018, listened to 1,300 marsquakes and measured the inside of Mars. Four years later, covered in dust, it stopped.
2021년 2월 옛 호수 바닥에 내려 돌 시료를 모으고 있습니다. 헬리콥: In February 2021 it landed on the bed of an old lake, where it gathers rock samples. The helicopter Ingenuity flew 72 times.
2021년 5월 중국의 첫 화성 탐사차 주룽이 내렸습니다. 1년 동안 1: In May 2021 Zhurong, China's first Mars rover, landed. It drove 1.9 km in a year and did not wake from its winter sleep.
1억 800만 년 전에 생긴 지름 85km 분화구입니다. 보름달에 사방으: A crater 85 km across made 108 million years ago. The white rays that spread across the full Moon come from here.
지름 93km, 깊이 3.8km의 분화구입니다. 계단처럼 층진 벽과 가운: A crater 93 km across and 3.8 km deep, with walls stepped like stairs and clear central peaks.
용암이 굳어 생긴 어두운 평원입니다. 1969년 사람이 처음 달에 내린: A dark plain of hardened lava. People first landed on the Moon, in 1969, in the south-west of this sea.
39억 년 전 큰 충돌로 생긴 지름 1,100km 분지에 용암이 찬 곳입: A basin 1,100 km across, made by a great impact 3.9 billion years ago and filled with lava. It is the largest round sea on the Moon's near side.
달에서 가장 넓은 바다로 남북으로 2,500km가 넘습니다. 달의 바다: The widest sea on the Moon, over 2,500 km from north to south. Alone among the Moon's seas it is called an ocean.
지름 약 2,500km, 깊이 8km로 달에서 가장 크고 오래된 충돌 분: About 2,500 km across and 8 km deep: the largest and oldest impact basin on the Moon. It takes up nearly all the south of the far side.
달 남극에 있는 지름 21km 분화구입니다. 바닥에 햇빛이 한 번도 들지: A crater 21 km across at the Moon's south pole. Sunlight has never reached its floor, so ice is thought to lie there.
비의 바다 가장자리를 따라 600km 뻗은 산맥입니다. 가장 높은 하위헌: A range running 600 km along the edge of the Sea of Rains. Its highest, Mons Huygens, is 5,500 m.
알프스 산맥을 가로지르는 길이 166km, 폭 10km의 곧은 골짜기입니: A straight valley 166 km long and 10 km wide that cuts across the lunar Alps.
길이 110km, 높이 약 300m의 곧은 단층 절벽입니다. 해가 낮게: A straight fault cliff 110 km long and about 300 m high. Under a low Sun it shows as a black line.
달 뒷면에 드문 바다입니다. 1959년 루나 3호가 처음 찍은 뒷면 사진: One of the few seas on the Moon's far side. It was found and named from the first photographs of the far side, taken by Luna 3 in 1959.
달 뒷면에서 가장 눈에 띄는 분화구입니다. 지름 185km 바닥에 검은: The most striking crater on the Moon's far side. Dark lava fills its floor, 185 km across, and a peak rises in the middle.
지름 670km쯤의 둥근 바다입니다. 지구에서 보면 달 토끼의 몸통 자리: A round sea about 670 km across. Seen from Earth it is the body of the Moon rabbit. Apollo 17 landed at its edge.
다른 바다와 떨어져 홀로 있는 지름 550km쯤의 둥근 바다입니다. 달: A round sea about 550 km across, standing apart from the other seas. At the Moon's eastern edge, it can be seen by eye.
지름 100km쯤의 분화구입니다. 바닥을 용암이 매끈하게 채워, 밝은 산: A crater about 100 km across. Lava filled its floor smooth, so it looks like a black lake among bright mountains.
달 앞면에서 가장 밝은 곳입니다. 지름 40km의 젊은 분화구로, 둘레보: The brightest place on the Moon's near side. A young crater 40 km across, it shines about twice as bright as the land round it.
A crater about 30 km across between the Ocean of Storms and the Sea of Islands. Its bright rays run over 300 km.
지름 231km로 달 앞면에서 손꼽히게 큰 분화구입니다. 2020년 이곳: At 231 km across, one of the largest craters on the near side. In 2020 water molecules were confirmed in sunlit ground here.
비의 바다 북서쪽에 반달 모양으로 파인 지름 250km쯤의 만입니다. 쥐: A bay about 250 km across, cut like a half moon into the north-west of the Sea of Rains. The Jura Mountains curve round it.
폭풍의 대양에 그려진 길이 70km쯤의 밝은 소용돌이 무늬입니다. 높낮이: A bright swirl about 70 km long drawn on the Ocean of Storms. The ground is flat: only the colour differs.
높이 22km, 지름 600km쯤의 화산입니다. 에베레스트의 두 배 반: A volcano about 22 km high and 600 km across. Two and a half times as high as Everest, it is the largest volcano known in the solar system.
길이 4,000km, 깊이 7km의 협곡입니다. 화성 둘레의 5분의 1을: A canyon 4,000 km long and 7 km deep. It crosses a fifth of the way round Mars and is nine times as long as the Grand Canyon.
높이 14 → 18km의 화산 셋이 700km 간격으로 한 줄로 서 있습: Three volcanoes 14 → 18 km high stand in a row 700 km apart. The middle one, Pavonis Mons, is on the equator.
지름 2,300km, 깊이 7km의 충돌 분지입니다. 화성에서 가장 낮은: An impact basin 2,300 km across and 7 km deep. It is the lowest place on Mars, and the air pressure on its floor is about twice the average.
지름 1,000km쯤의 얼음 모자입니다. 두께 2km의 물 얼음 위에,: A cap of ice about 1,000 km across. On water ice 2 km thick, about 1 m of dry ice settles every winter.
화성 남극의 얼음 모자입니다. 물 얼음 위에 드라이아이스가 덮여 있고,: The ice cap at Mars's south pole. Dry ice lies over water ice, and that layer does not all go even in summer.
지름 82km의 분화구에 두께 1.8km의 물 얼음이 한 해 내내 녹지: A crater 82 km across, filled all year with water ice 1.8 km thick that never melts.
1976년 바이킹 1호의 사진에서 사람 얼굴처럼 보인 길이 2km쯤의 언: A hill about 2 km long that looked like a human face in a Viking 1 photograph of 1976. Later, sharper photographs showed an ordinary hill.
1659년 하위헌스가 망원경으로 보고 그린, 다른 행성의 지형으로는 처음: Seen and drawn by Huygens through a telescope in 1659: the first feature recorded on another planet. It is a dark volcanic land of basalt.
추류모프-게라시멘코 혜성의 핵 300km 안을 지나기: Pass within 300 km of the core of Comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko
On November 12, 2014, Rosetta's lander Philae set down on this comet: the first probe to land on a comet.
목성 남반구(남위 44도) 구름 꼭대기의 충돌 자리 20,000km 안에: Touch the cloud tops within 20,000 km of the impact site in Jupiter's southern half (44° S)
토성 북극(북위 78도) 구름 꼭대기의 육각형 15,000km 안에 닿기: Touch the cloud tops within 15,000 km of the hexagon at Saturn's north pole (78° N)
해왕성 남반구 구름 꼭대기의 검은 점 10,000km 안에 닿기: Touch the cloud tops within 10,000 km of the dark spot in Neptune's southern half
1979년 3월 보이저 1호가 이오에서 솟는 연기를 찍었습니다. 지구 밖: In March 1979 Voyager 1 photographed a plume rising from Io: the first active volcano found off the Earth.
2005년 카시니가 남극의 네 줄 균열에서 물과 얼음이 뿜어 나오는 것을: In 2005 Cassini found water and ice spouting from four cracks at the south pole.
1994년 7월, 스물한 조각으로 부서진 혜성이 목성 남반구에 차례로 부: In July 1994 a comet broken into twenty-one pieces struck Jupiter's southern half one after another.
1982년 3월 1일 금성에 내려 127분을 버텼습니다. 금성 표면의 첫: It landed on Venus on March 1, 1982, and lasted 127 minutes. It took the first colour photographs of the surface of Venus.
2015년 뉴허라이즌스가 찍은 하트 모양의 밝은 땅입니다. 명왕성을 찾은: The bright heart-shaped land photographed by New Horizons in 2015. It is named after Tombaugh, who found Pluto.
1981년 보이저 2호의 사진에 토성 북극의 여섯 변짜리 구름 띠가 찍혔: Voyager 2's photographs of 1981 showed a six-sided band of cloud at Saturn's north pole. Each side is longer than Earth is wide.
2022년 6월 21일 이곳에서 누리호가 위성을 궤도에 올렸습니다. 한국: On June 21, 2022, the rocket Nuri put satellites in orbit from here: the first time with a launcher built in Korea.
수성을 처음으로 돌던 메신저가 연료가 다해 2015년 4월 30일 이곳에: MESSENGER, the first to orbit Mercury, ran out of fuel and fell here on April 30, 2015.
얼음판이 부서져 떠다니다 다시 언 모양입니다. 얼음 아래에 바다가 있다는: It looks like plates of ice that broke, drifted and froze again: counted as a clue to a sea under the ice.
1970년 12월 15일 금성에 내려 23분 동안 신호를 보냈습니다. 다: It landed on Venus on December 15, 1970, and sent signals for 23 minutes: the first signal from the surface of another planet.
2015년 던이 이 충돌구 바닥의 밝은 점을 찍었습니다. 땅속 소금물이: In 2015 Dawn photographed the bright spots on this crater's floor: sodium carbonate left by salt water risen from underground.
1969년 7월 16일 아폴로 11호가 이 발사대에서 떠났습니다. 나흘: Apollo 11 left from this pad on July 16, 1969. Four days later it landed on the Moon.
2007년 카시니가 찾은 타이탄에서 가장 큰 바다입니다. 물이 아니라 메: The largest sea on Titan, found by Cassini in 2007. It is filled not with water but with methane and ethane.
카론의 북극은 붉은 갈색입니다. 명왕성에서 빠져나온 기체가 얼어붙고 햇빛: Charon's north pole is reddish brown. Gas that escaped from Pluto is thought to have frozen there and been changed by sunlight.
1989년 보이저 2호가 지구만 한 검은 폭풍을 찍었습니다. 1994년: In 1989 Voyager 2 photographed a dark storm the size of Earth. When Hubble looked again in 1994 it was gone.
해왕성 구름 꼭대기 5,000km 안을 지나기: Pass within 5,000 km of Neptune's cloud tops
1989년 8월 25일 보이저 2호가 해왕성 구름 위 4,950km를 지: On August 25, 1989, Voyager 2 passed 4,950 km above Neptune's clouds. It is the only spacecraft to have been to Neptune.
천왕성 구름 꼭대기 81,500km 안을 지나기: Pass within 81,500 km of Uranus's cloud tops
1986년 1월 24일 보이저 2호가 천왕성 구름 위 81,500km를: On January 24, 1986, Voyager 2 passed 81,500 km above Uranus's clouds. It is the only spacecraft to have been to Uranus.
국제우주정거장 3,000km 안까지 가기: Go to within 3,000 km of the International Space Station

The Sun is about 1.39 million km across: 109 Earths in a row. It shines by fusion, turning hydrogen into helium; its centre is at about 15 million degrees and its surface at about 5,500. Strangely the corona, its outer air, is over a million degrees, and the Parker Solar Probe is flying through the corona to find out why.
태양의 빛이 지구에 닿는 데에는 약 8분 20초가 걸립니다. 나이는 약: Its light takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth. It is about 4.6 billion years old and will burn for about 5 billion more. The dark spots on its surface (sunspots) are cooler than what is round them, and their number rises and falls about every 11 years.
수성은 태양에 가장 가까운 행성이고 여덟 행성 가운데 가장 작습니다. 지: Mercury is the planet nearest the Sun and the smallest of the eight. At 4,879 km across it is about 1.4 times the Moon. With almost no air to hold heat, the day reaches 430 degrees and the night drops to minus 180.
태양을 88일에 한 바퀴 돌지만 자전은 59일이 걸려, 태양을 두 바퀴: It goes round the Sun in 88 days but turns in 59, so it turns exactly three times for every two trips round the Sun. That makes it 176 days from one sunrise to the next. There is ice in polar craters where sunlight never comes. Mariner 10 first passed it in 1974, and MESSENGER circled it for four years from 2011, making its map.
금성은 크기가 지구와 비슷해 쌍둥이 행성으로 불리지만 표면은 전혀 다릅니: Venus is called Earth's twin for its size, but its surface is nothing like Earth's. Thick air of carbon dioxide traps the heat: the surface is at about 465 degrees, hotter than Mercury, which is nearer the Sun. The pressure is about 90 times Earth's, the same as 900 m down in the sea.
하늘은 황산 구름으로 덮여 있어 표면이 보이지 않고, 레이더로 지도를 만: Clouds of sulfuric acid cover the sky and hide the surface, so its map was made by radar. It turns the opposite way to the other planets, so the Sun rises in the west. From Earth it is the brightest thing after the Sun and the Moon: the morning star and the evening star. The Soviet Venera probes landed and sent photographs; the longest any lasted was 127 minutes.
지구는 표면에 액체 물이 있고 생명이 확인된 하나뿐인 천체입니다. 지름: Earth is the only body with liquid water on its surface and the only one known to have life. It is 12,742 km across and 71% of its surface is sea. Its air is 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.
자전축이 23.4도 기울어 있어 계절이 생깁니다. 자기장이 태양에서 날아: Its axis is tipped 23.4 degrees, which makes the seasons. Its magnetic field holds off particles flying from the Sun, and those particles strike the air near the poles and make auroras. It is about 4.54 billion years old. In the photograph Voyager 1 took from 6 billion km away in 1990, Earth was smaller than a dot.
달은 지구의 하나뿐인 위성이고 지름 3,475km로 지구의 4분의 1쯤입: The Moon is Earth's only moon; at 3,475 km across it is about a quarter of Earth. It is thought to have formed about 4.5 billion years ago from the rubble thrown out when a body the size of Mars struck Earth. Its gravity is a sixth of Earth's.
공전과 자전이 모두 27.3일이라 지구에는 늘 같은 면만 보입니다. 어둡: It goes round and turns in the same 27.3 days, so Earth always sees the same face. The dark "seas" are not water but plains of old hardened lava. With no air, footprints do not wear away. Twelve Apollo astronauts walked there from 1969 to 1972, and the mirrors they left are still used to measure the distance: that is how we know the Moon moves away 3.8 cm every year.
화성은 지름 6,779km로 지구의 절반쯤입니다. 흙에 산화철, 곧 녹이: Mars is 6,779 km across, about half of Earth. Its soil is full of iron oxide, which is rust, and so it looks red. Its air is thin, about a hundredth of Earth's, and mostly carbon dioxide. Its day is 24 hours 37 minutes, much like Earth's, and its axis is tipped 25 degrees, so it has seasons.
태양계에서 가장 높은 화산 올림푸스산(약 22km)과 가장 큰 협곡 마리: It has the highest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons (about 22 km), and the largest canyon, Valles Marineris (about 4,000 km long). Dried river beds and lake floors remain, so water is thought to have flowed long ago. There is still ice at the poles and under the ground. It has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.
포보스는 화성의 두 위성 가운데 큰 쪽이지만 긴 쪽이 27km인 감자 모: Phobos is the larger of Mars's two moons, yet it is a small potato-shaped body 27 km long. It goes round about 6,000 km above Mars every 7 hours 39 minutes. That is faster than Mars turns, so seen from Mars it rises in the west and sets in the east.
지름 9km의 큰 분화구 스티크니가 있습니다. 화성의 조석력 때문에 10: It has a big crater 9 km across called Stickney. Mars's tides draw it about 1.8 m nearer every hundred years; in tens of millions of years it will break into a ring or fall on Mars. Asaph Hall found it in 1877.
데이모스는 화성의 작은 위성으로 긴 쪽이 15km쯤입니다. 화성 중심에서: Deimos is the smaller moon of Mars, about 15 km long. It goes round about 23,000 km from the centre of Mars every 30 hours 18 minutes. From the surface of Mars it looks like a bright star with no size.
표면은 고운 먼지로 덮여 분화구들이 반쯤 묻혀 있어 포보스보다 매끈합니다: Fine dust covers its surface and half buries its craters, so it is smoother than Phobos. Unlike Phobos it is very slowly moving away from Mars. Some think both are captured asteroids and some that they are rubble from a great impact; it is not settled. Asaph Hall found it in 1877, together with Phobos.
목성은 태양계에서 가장 큰 행성입니다. 지름 약 14만km로 지구 11개: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system. It is about 140,000 km across, 11 Earths in a row, and has 318 times Earth's mass. It is a gas planet, mostly hydrogen and helium, with no ground to stand on.
자전이 9시간 56분으로 행성 가운데 가장 빨라, 구름이 띠 모양으로 늘: It turns in 9 hours 56 minutes, the fastest of the planets, which draws its clouds out into bands. The Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has lasted at least 190 years, though it is slowly shrinking. It has over 110 known moons; the four large ones (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) were found by Galileo in 1610. It also has faint rings.
이오는 태양계에서 화산 활동이 가장 활발한 천체입니다. 지름 3,643k: Io is the most volcanic body in the solar system. At 3,643 km across it is a little larger than the Moon, and it has over 400 active volcanoes. Jupiter and the neighbouring moons pull on it in turn, kneading its inside and heating it.
표면은 화산이 뿜은 황 때문에 노랗고 붉습니다. 용암이 계속 덮어서 충돌: Its surface is yellow and red with the sulfur its volcanoes spout. Lava keeps covering it, so it has almost no impact craters. In 1979 a rising volcanic plume was found in a photograph by Voyager 1: the first active volcano seen off the Earth. It goes round Jupiter in 1.77 days.
유로파는 지름 3,122km로 달보다 조금 작습니다. 표면은 물 얼음으로: Europa is 3,122 km across, a little smaller than the Moon. Covered in water ice, it is among the smoothest bodies in the solar system. Cracks run over the ice like a net.
Under the shell of ice there is thought to be a sea of salt water about 100 km deep, holding about twice as much water as all Earth's seas. That puts it first among places to look for life beyond Earth. Europa Clipper, which left in 2024, arrives in 2030 and will skim past many times. It goes round Jupiter in 3.55 days.
가니메데는 태양계에서 가장 큰 위성입니다. 지름 5,268km로 행성인: Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system. At 5,268 km across it is larger than the planet Mercury, though with so much ice it has less than half Mercury's mass.
위성 가운데 하나뿐으로 스스로 자기장을 가지고 있고, 그래서 오로라도 생: Alone among moons it has a magnetic field of its own, and so it has auroras too. Its surface is a mix of old dark land and bright grooved land. A sea is thought to lie deep under the ice. Europe's Juice probe left in 2023 and in the 2030s will be the first to orbit Ganymede. It goes round Jupiter in 7.15 days.
칼리스토는 지름 4,821km로 수성과 거의 같은 크기입니다. 태양계에서: Callisto is 4,821 km across, almost the size of Mercury. It is among the most cratered bodies in the solar system, and its surface has hardly changed in about 4 billion years.
가장 큰 흔적은 발할라로, 가운데 밝은 곳을 둘러싼 고리 무늬가 지름 3: Its largest scar is Valhalla: rings round a bright centre spread out to 3,800 km across. It is the farthest of the four Galilean moons from Jupiter, where the radiation is weak, so it is the place named if people ever build a base near Jupiter. It goes round Jupiter in 16.7 days.
토성은 둘째로 큰 행성으로 지름이 약 11만 6천km입니다. 평균 밀도가: Saturn is the second largest planet, about 116,000 km across. Its average density is less than water's (0.69 g per cubic cm): given a sea big enough, it would float. Like Jupiter it is a gas planet of hydrogen and helium.
고리는 대부분 물 얼음 알갱이이고, 끝에서 끝까지 28만km에 이르지만: Its rings are mostly grains of water ice. They reach 280,000 km from edge to edge, yet are mostly only tens of metres thick. At the north pole is a six-sided pattern of cloud with sides longer than Earth is wide. It has over 290 known moons, more than any other planet. Cassini circled and studied it from 2004 to 2017.
미마스는 지름 396km로, 제 무게로 둥글어진 천체 가운데 가장 작은: Mimas is 396 km across, among the smallest bodies pulled round by their own weight. Its big crater Herschel, about 130 km across, makes people say it looks like the space fortress in a film. The peak in the middle of the crater is about 6 km high.
It is nearly all water ice. It goes round Saturn in 22.6 hours. Its gravity tugs at the grains of the rings and makes the Cassini Division, the widest gap in Saturn's rings. William Herschel found it in 1789.
엔셀라두스는 지름 504km의 작은 얼음 위성입니다. 표면이 새 얼음으로: Enceladus is a small icy moon 504 km across. Fresh ice covers its surface and sends back nearly all the sunlight, making it the whitest body in the solar system.
2005년 카시니가 남극의 갈라진 틈 \"호랑이 줄무늬\"에서 물과 얼음: In 2005 Cassini found water and grains of ice spouting from the "tiger stripes", cracks at the south pole. That means a sea under the ice. The ice it spouts becomes Saturn's E ring. Cassini flew through the jets and found salt, organic matter and hydrogen, which is why it is counted a place to look for life. It goes round Saturn in 1.37 days.
Tethys is 1,062 km across and nearly pure water ice. Its density is almost the same as water's.
지름 445km의 분화구 오디세우스가 있는데, 테티스 지름의 5분의 2에: It has the crater Odysseus, 445 km across, two fifths as wide as Tethys itself. And Ithaca Chasma, a canyon 2,000 km long and up to 100 km wide, wraps three quarters of the way round the moon. Two small moons, Telesto and Calypso, share its orbit 60 degrees ahead and behind. It goes round Saturn in 1.89 days; Cassini found it in 1684.
디오네는 지름 1,123km의 얼음 위성입니다. 얼음 속에 바위 심이 있: Dione is an icy moon 1,123 km across. With a core of rock inside the ice it is heavier than Tethys.
뒤쪽 반구에는 밝은 줄무늬가 있는데, 가까이에서 보니 높이 수백 m의 얼: Its trailing half has bright streaks, which from close by turned out to be ice cliffs hundreds of metres high. Two small moons, Helene and Polydeuces, share its orbit 60 degrees ahead and behind. It goes round Saturn in 2.74 days; Cassini found it in 1684.
레아는 토성에서 둘째로 큰 위성으로 지름이 1,527km입니다. 물 얼음: Rhea is Saturn's second largest moon, 1,527 km across. It is three quarters water ice and one quarter rock.
표면은 분화구로 빽빽하게 덮여 있고, 뒤쪽 반구에는 디오네처럼 밝은 얼음: Its surface is thick with craters, and its trailing half has streaks of bright ice cliffs like Dione's. It has very thin air of oxygen and carbon dioxide. It goes round Saturn in 4.52 days; Cassini found it in 1672.
Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the second largest in the solar system after Ganymede. At 5,150 km across it is larger than Mercury. Alone among moons it has thick air, mostly nitrogen, with 1.5 times Earth's pressure at the surface.
표면 온도는 영하 179도입니다. 이 추위에서는 메탄과 에탄이 액체라,: The surface is at minus 179 degrees. In that cold, methane and ethane are liquids: they rain, run in rivers and fill lakes and seas. It is the only body besides Earth with liquid standing on its surface. Orange haze hid the surface until Huygens photographed river channels on its way down in 2005. The drone probe Dragonfly is to go there. It goes round Saturn in 15.9 days.
이아페투스는 지름 1,469km이고, 한쪽 반구는 숯처럼 검고 반대쪽은: Iapetus is 1,469 km across; one half is black as charcoal and the other white as snow. Cassini, who found it in 1671, guessed rightly that it showed on only one side of Saturn because its two sides differ in brightness.
검은 쪽은 공전하며 앞서 나가는 면으로, 바깥 위성에서 온 어두운 먼지를: The dark side is the one that leads as it goes round, coated by dark dust from the outer moons. A ridge over 13 km high runs 1,300 km along its equator and makes it look like a walnut. It lies 3.56 million km from Saturn and goes round in 79 days.
천왕성은 지름 약 5만km로 지구의 4배입니다. 자전축이 98도 누워 있: Uranus is about 50,000 km across, four times Earth. Its axis is tipped 98 degrees, so it goes round the Sun rolling on its side. At the poles that means 42 years of day and 42 of night. It is thought to have been knocked over long ago by a large body.
물, 암모니아, 메탄의 얼음이 많아 얼음 거인으로 부릅니다. 대기의 메탄: With so much ice of water, ammonia and methane it is called an ice giant. Methane in its air soaks up red light, so it looks blue-green. It was the first planet found by telescope, by William Herschel in 1781. Only one spacecraft has been near: Voyager 2 in 1986. It has 13 rings and nearly 30 moons. It goes round the Sun in 84 years.
미란다는 천왕성의 큰 위성 다섯 가운데 가장 작아 지름이 472km입니다: Miranda is the smallest of the five large moons of Uranus, 472 km across. Its surface looks like a patchwork of different lands sewn together: grooved land, cratered land and chevron shapes side by side.
베로나 절벽은 높이가 20km쯤으로 태양계에서 가장 높은 절벽으로 꼽힙니: The cliff Verona Rupes, about 20 km high, is counted the tallest in the solar system. Gravity is so weak that a fall from it would take about 12 minutes to reach the bottom. The only photographs are of its southern half, taken as Voyager 2 passed in 1986. It goes round Uranus in 1.41 days; Kuiper found it in 1948.
아리엘은 지름 1,158km이고 천왕성의 큰 위성 가운데 표면이 가장 밝: Ariel is 1,158 km across and has the brightest surface of the large moons of Uranus. It has few craters and a tangle of long valleys, so its surface is thought to be fairly young.
The valley floors are smooth, it is thought, because ice flowed like lava and filled them. The only photographs are those Voyager 2 took in 1986, showing a third of its surface. It goes round Uranus in 2.52 days; William Lassell found it in 1851. The moons of Uranus are named from the works of Shakespeare and Pope.
움브리엘은 지름 1,169km로 아리엘과 크기가 거의 같지만 훨씬 어둡습: Umbriel is 1,169 km across, almost the size of Ariel but far darker: the darkest of the large moons of Uranus.
표면은 오래된 분화구로 덮여 있어 오랫동안 바뀌지 않았다고 봅니다. 밝은: Old craters cover its surface, which is thought to have stayed unchanged for a long time. It has a bright ringed crater called Wunda; what makes it bright is not yet known. It goes round Uranus in 4.14 days; Lassell found it in 1851, together with Ariel.
티타니아는 천왕성의 가장 큰 위성으로 지름이 1,577km입니다. 얼음과: Titania is the largest moon of Uranus, 1,577 km across. It is about half ice and half rock.
길이 1,500km에 이르는 메시나 협곡을 비롯해 큰 골짜기들이 있는데,: It has great valleys, among them the canyon Messina Chasmata, 1,500 km long: marks, it is thought, of the crust splitting as the inside froze and swelled. It goes round Uranus in 8.7 days. William Herschel found it in 1787, together with Oberon. Its name is the fairy queen of Shakespeare's "A Midsummer Night's Dream".
오베론은 천왕성의 큰 위성 가운데 가장 바깥을 돌고, 지름 1,523km: Oberon is the outermost of the large moons of Uranus and the second largest, 1,523 km across.
표면은 분화구가 가장 많아 가장 오래된 땅으로 봅니다. 몇몇 분화구 바닥: Its surface has the most craters and is thought the oldest. Dark stuff lies on the floors of some craters, and at its edge stands a mountain about 11 km high. It goes round Uranus in 13.5 days. William Herschel found it in 1787; its name is the fairy king of "A Midsummer Night's Dream".
해왕성은 태양에서 가장 먼 행성으로, 지구보다 30배 멀리 있습니다. 지: Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun, 30 times as far as Earth. It is about 49,000 km across, 3.9 times Earth. One trip round the Sun takes 165 years: found in 1846, it finished its first lap only in 2011.
천왕성의 움직임이 계산과 어긋나는 것을 보고 수학으로 자리를 먼저 셈한: It was found after its place was worked out by mathematics, from the way Uranus strayed from its reckoned path. Its winds pass 2,000 km an hour, the fastest in the solar system. In 1989 Voyager 2 photographed the Great Dark Spot, a dark storm the size of Earth, but when Hubble looked a few years later it was gone. Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have been near.
트리톤은 해왕성의 가장 큰 위성으로 지름이 2,707km입니다. 큰 위성: Triton is Neptune's largest moon, 2,707 km across. Alone among large moons it goes round against its planet's spin. So it is thought to be a body from the Kuiper belt that Neptune captured.
표면 온도는 영하 235도로 태양계에서 가장 추운 곳에 듭니다. 그런데도: Its surface is at minus 235 degrees, among the coldest places in the solar system. Even so, in 1989 Voyager 2 photographed geysers of nitrogen gas and dark dust rising 8 km. Part of the surface is bumpy like the skin of a melon. It is slowly nearing Neptune and in billions of years will break up into a ring. It goes round Neptune in 5.88 days.
세레스는 화성과 목성 사이 소행성대에서 가장 큰 천체로 지름이 약 940: Ceres is the largest body in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, about 940 km across. It holds about a third of the belt's whole mass. Piazzi found it on January 1, 1801, and at first it was called a planet. Since 2006 it has been classed as a dwarf planet.
2015년 던 탐사선이 도착해 3년 넘게 돌았습니다. 왜행성에 간 첫 탐: The Dawn probe arrived in 2015 and circled it for over three years: the first spacecraft at a dwarf planet. The bright spots in Occator Crater were salt left by salt water risen from underground. There is much ice inside, and Ahuna Mons, a lone mountain 4 km high, is thought to be an ice volcano. It goes round the Sun in 4.6 years and its day is 9 hours.
명왕성은 지름 2,377km로 달의 3분의 2 크기입니다. 1930년 클: Pluto is 2,377 km across, two thirds the size of the Moon. Clyde Tombaugh found it in 1930 and it was called the ninth planet until 2006, when it was classed again as a dwarf planet, because bodies of about its size kept being found in the Kuiper belt.
2015년 뉴허라이즌스가 지나가며 찍은 사진에는 하트 모양의 밝은 땅이: The photographs New Horizons took as it passed in 2015 showed a bright heart-shaped land. Its left half, Sputnik Planitia, is a glacier of nitrogen ice slowly churning. There are mountains of water ice over 3 km high and thin layers of blue haze. It goes round the Sun in 248 years, on an orbit so long that for about 20 years it is nearer the Sun than Neptune.
카론은 명왕성의 가장 큰 위성으로 지름이 1,212km입니다. 명왕성 지: Charon is Pluto's largest moon, 1,212 km across. At over half Pluto's width, the two are more twin worlds than planet and moon. The point they circle lies in empty space outside Pluto.
둘은 6.39일에 한 바퀴씩 서로 마주 보며 돕니다. 그래서 명왕성의 한: They go round every 6.39 days, always facing each other. So from one side of Pluto Charon hangs always in the same place in the sky, and from the other side it is never seen. The red stain at its north pole is thought to be gas from Pluto, frozen there and changed by sunlight. James Christy found it in 1978.
핼리 혜성은 약 76년마다 돌아오는 혜성입니다. 1705년 에드먼드 핼리: Halley's Comet comes back about every 76 years. In 1705 Edmond Halley worked out that comets in old records were one and the same and named the year of its return. The oldest record is from China in 240 BC.
핵은 길이 15km, 폭 8km쯤의 땅콩 모양이고 숯보다 검습니다. 태양: Its core is shaped like a peanut, about 15 km long and 8 km wide, and blacker than charcoal. Near the Sun its ice turns to gas and spouts out to make the tail, which always points away from the Sun. When it passed in 1986 Europe's Giotto came within 596 km and photographed the core from close by. It is next nearest the Sun in July 2061. The meteor showers of May and October each year are crumbs this comet has shed.
헤일-밥 혜성은 1995년 7월 23일 앨런 헤일과 토머스 밥이 따로따로: Comet Hale-Bopp was found on July 23, 1995, by Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp, each on his own. It was already beyond Jupiter then, and so large that it could be seen even so. Its core is about 60 km across, several times Halley's.
1997년 봄에 가장 밝았고, 18개월 동안 맨눈으로 보여 기록을 세웠습: It was brightest in the spring of 1997 and was seen by eye for 18 months, a record. It showed even in city skies and is counted the comet seen by the most people in the 20th century. Its blue gas tail and yellowish dust tail stood clearly apart. Its orbit is very long: it next returns around the year 4380.
추류모프-게라시멘코 혜성은 1969년 클림 추류모프와 스베틀라나 게라시멘: Comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko was found in 1969 by Klim Churyumov and Svetlana Gerasimenko. It goes round the Sun in 6.4 years. Its core is shaped like a rubber duck, a large lump joined to a small one, about 4 km long: two bodies thought to have met slowly and stuck.
유럽의 로제타 탐사선이 10년을 날아 2014년에 도착해 2년 동안 곁을: Europe's Rosetta probe flew ten years, arrived in 2014 and circled it for two: the first spacecraft to orbit a comet. The lander Philae came down on November 12, 2014, but its harpoons did not hold; it bounced twice and stopped in shadow. It was the first lander on a comet. This comet's water was not of the same make as the water of Earth's seas.
보이저 1호는 1977년 9월 5일에 떠났습니다. 1979년 목성을 지나: Voyager 1 left on September 5, 1977. Passing Jupiter in 1979 it found the volcanoes of Io, and in 1980 it passed Saturn and Titan. Bending its path for a close look at Titan took it out of the plane of the planets, and it could visit no more of them.
1990년 2월 14일 60억km 밖에서 뒤돌아 태양계 가족사진을 찍었고: On February 14, 1990, from 6 billion km away, it turned and took the family portrait of the solar system; the Earth in it is the "Pale Blue Dot". In August 2012 it left the reach of the solar wind and became the first spacecraft in the space between the stars. It carries a golden record of Earth's sounds and greetings in 55 languages. As its plutonium battery weakens, its instruments are being switched off one by one.
Voyager 2 left on August 20, 1977, 16 days before Voyager 1. It passed Jupiter (1979), Saturn (1981), Uranus (1986) and Neptune (1989) in turn. The four planets line up on one side only about once in 175 years, which let it borrow each planet's gravity to reach the next.
천왕성과 해왕성에 가 본 탐사선은 지금까지 이것 하나입니다. 천왕성에서: It is still the only spacecraft to have been to Uranus and Neptune. It found ten new moons at Uranus and six at Neptune. In November 2018 it entered the space between the stars. It carries the same golden record as Voyager 1.
허블 우주망원경은 1990년 4월 우주왕복선 디스커버리호에 실려 올라갔습: The Hubble Space Telescope went up in April 1990 aboard the space shuttle Discovery. Once up, its 2.4 m mirror proved to have been ground wrong by a fiftieth of the width of a hair, and its pictures were blurred. In 1993 astronauts went up and fitted a device that worked as its glasses.
대기 밖에 있어 별빛이 흔들리지 않습니다. 우주가 점점 빠르게 팽창한다는: Above the air, starlight does not shimmer. It helped show that the universe is growing faster and faster, and narrowed the universe's age to about 13.8 billion years. The "Hubble Deep Field", ten days' exposure of an empty patch of sky, showed thousands of galaxies. Astronauts went up five times to mend it, last in 2009. It is named after Edwin Hubble, who found that the universe is growing.
제임스 웹 우주망원경은 2021년 12월 25일 아리안 5 로켓으로 떠났: The James Webb Space Telescope left on December 25, 2021, on an Ariane 5 rocket. Folded to fit the rocket, it spent two weeks unfolding in space and reached its place a month after leaving. Eighteen six-sided golden mirrors make one mirror 6.5 m across.
적외선을 보는 망원경이라 제 몸의 열도 방해가 됩니다. 그래서 테니스장만: It sees infrared, so even its own warmth gets in the way. A five-layer sunshield the size of a tennis court blocks the light of the Sun and Earth and cools it to about minus 230 degrees. Its place is the L2 point, 1.5 million km from Earth, where the Sun and Earth are always on the same side and can be shaded at once. It looks at galaxies from when the universe was only a few hundred million years old, and at what the air of exoplanets is made of.
케플러 우주망원경은 2009년 3월에 떠나 지구 뒤를 따라 태양을 돌았습: The Kepler Space Telescope left in March 2009 and trailed Earth round the Sun. For four years without rest it watched about 150,000 stars in one patch of sky toward Cygnus and Lyra.
행성이 별 앞을 지나면 별빛이 아주 조금 어두워집니다. 지구만 한 행성이: When a planet crosses its star the starlight dims a very little: for a planet the size of Earth, by about one part in ten thousand. By that change Kepler found over 2,600 exoplanets and showed that our galaxy holds more planets than stars. In 2013 a wheel that steadied it failed, but it went on observing by leaning on the pressure of sunlight, and in 2018, out of fuel, it retired.
찬드라 X선 망원경은 1999년 7월 우주왕복선 컬럼비아호에 실려 올라갔: The Chandra X-ray Observatory went up in July 1999 aboard the space shuttle Columbia: the heaviest load a shuttle ever carried. X-rays cannot pass through Earth's air and can only be seen from space.
X선은 거울을 정면으로 만나면 뚫고 들어가므로, 통 모양의 거울 네 겹에: X-rays go straight through a mirror they meet head-on, so they are gathered by glancing off four nested barrel-shaped mirrors. It looks at places hotter than millions of degrees: the surroundings of black holes, the remains of supernovas, the gas between galaxies in clusters. To keep clear of Earth's radiation belts it flies a long orbit of 64 hours. It is named after Chandrasekhar, who studied the deaths of stars.
유클리드 우주망원경은 유럽우주국이 2023년 7월에 올렸습니다. 제임스: The Euclid space telescope was launched by the European Space Agency in July 2023. Like Webb it circles the L2 point, 1.5 million km from Earth. Its 1.2 m mirror takes in a patch of sky wider than two full Moons at a time.
6년 동안 하늘의 3분의 1을 찍어 은하 수십억 개의 모양과 거리를 잽니: Over six years it photographs a third of the sky and measures the shapes and distances of billions of galaxies. The shapes of far galaxies are bent a little by the gravity of matter in front of them, and measuring that bending shows where the unseen dark matter lies. Its aim is a map of the dark matter and dark energy that make up 95% of the universe.
The International Space Station was built together by the United States, Russia, Europe, Japan and Canada. The first module went up in 1998, and the pieces, carried up on more than 40 flights, were joined in space. At 109 m long it is the size of a football field, and it weighs about 420 tonnes.
It flies 420 km above Earth at 7.7 km a second and goes round in 92 minutes, so the Sun rises 16 times a day. People have lived on it without a break since November 2000. They test how bodies and materials change where no weight is felt. In 2008 Yi So-yeon stayed here, the first Korean to do so. The plan is to end its work around 2030 and drop it into the sea.
톈궁은 중국이 혼자 지은 우주정거장입니다. 2021년 4월 중심 모듈 톈: Tiangong is the space station China built alone. The core module Tianhe went up in April 2021, and in 2022 the laboratory modules Wentian and Mengtian joined it to make a T. It weighs about 100 tonnes, about a quarter of the International Space Station.
지구 390km쯤 위를 돕니다. 우주비행사 셋이 여섯 달씩 머물고, 교대: It goes round about 390 km above Earth. Three astronauts stay for six months at a time, and at a handover six live there together. Tiangong means "palace in the sky".
Sputnik 1 was the first satellite, launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957: an aluminium ball 58 cm across weighing 83.6 kg, with four antennas. It went round Earth every 96 minutes.
싣고 있던 것은 송신기와 전지뿐이었고, \"삐, 삐\" 하는 신호를 21: All it carried was a transmitter and batteries, and it sent its "beep, beep" for 21 days. Radio amateurs all over the world could hear it. Three months later, on January 4, 1958, it came down into the air and burned up. This small ball began the space race, and the next year the United States founded NASA. Sputnik means "travelling companion".
화성 정찰 궤도선은 2005년 8월에 떠나 2006년 3월 화성에 도착했: The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter left in August 2005 and reached Mars in March 2006. It goes round over the poles about 300 km above Mars.
지름 50cm의 망원 카메라 하이라이즈는 화성 표면을 한 점에 30cm로: Its telescopic camera HiRISE, 50 cm across, photographs the surface at 30 cm to a dot and can make out things about 1 m across. It has caught rover tracks and parachutes, new craters, and dark streaks running down slopes. It also looks for buried ice by radar. And it relays to Earth what the rovers on the surface send.
Juno left in August 2011 and reached Jupiter on July 4, 2016. Sunlight at Jupiter is only a twenty-fifth of what Earth gets, yet it makes its power with three solar wings 9 m long.
목성의 극 위를 지나는 길쭉한 궤도를 돌며, 가장 가까울 때는 구름 위: It flies a long orbit over Jupiter's poles, coming down at its nearest to about 4,000 km above the clouds. To stand the fierce radiation its electronics sit in a box of titanium. It found storms the size of Earth gathered in rings at the poles, and learned that Jupiter's inside is more blurred and mixed than was thought. It is named after the goddess Juno, who saw through clouds.
카시니는 1997년 10월에 떠나 7년을 날아 2004년 토성에 도착했습: Cassini left in October 1997 and flew seven years to reach Saturn in 2004. Over 13 years it went round Saturn 294 times. The lander it carried, Huygens, set down on Titan in January 2005.
엔셀라두스의 물기둥과 타이탄의 메탄 호수를 찾았고, 고리의 알갱이와 북극: It found the jets of Enceladus and the methane lakes of Titan, and photographed the grains of the rings and the six-sided storm at the north pole from close by. As its fuel ran low it was sent into Saturn's air on September 15, 2017, so that it would not fall on and soil a moon that may hold life. Until just before it burned up it measured the air and sent what it found. It is named after the astronomer who found four of Saturn's moons and the gap in the rings.
파커 태양 탐사선은 2018년 8월에 떠났습니다. 금성을 일곱 번 스쳐: The Parker Solar Probe left in August 2018. Skimming past Venus seven times to shed speed, it has come closer to the Sun step by step. In December 2024 it came within about 6.1 million km of the Sun's surface.
그때 속도는 초속 190km가 넘어, 사람이 만든 것 가운데 가장 빠릅니: Its speed then was over 190 km a second, the fastest of anything people have made. A carbon shield 11 cm thick covers its front: the face of the shield stands 1,400 degrees and keeps the instruments behind it at about 30. It is trying to learn why the corona is hotter than the surface and how the solar wind is sped up. It is named after Eugene Parker, who foretold the solar wind: the first NASA spacecraft named after a living person.
테슬라 로드스터는 2018년 2월 6일 팰컨 헤비 로켓의 첫 시험 발사에: The Tesla Roadster is a red electric car that went up on February 6, 2018, on the first test flight of the Falcon Heavy rocket. A new rocket's first flight usually carries a lump of iron or concrete; this one carried the car Elon Musk used to drive.
운전석에는 우주복을 입힌 마네킹 \"스타맨\"이 앉아 있습니다. 태양을: At the wheel sits "Starman", a dummy in a spacesuit. It goes round the Sun every 557 days, at its farthest beyond the orbit of Mars. It has no science instruments. By reckoning there is a small chance it will hit Earth or Venus within tens of millions of years.
뉴허라이즌스는 2006년 1월에 떠났습니다. 떠날 때 초속 16km가 넘: New Horizons left in January 2006. Leaving at over 16 km a second, it was the fastest thing ever to leave Earth: it crossed the Moon's orbit in nine hours. After nine and a half years it passed Pluto at 12,500 km on July 14, 2015.
명왕성의 하트 모양 얼음 평원과 얼음 산, 카론의 붉은 극을 처음 찍었습: It took the first photographs of Pluto's heart-shaped plain of ice, its mountains of ice and Charon's red pole. Pluto was a planet when it left and a dwarf planet before it arrived. On January 1, 2019, it passed Arrokoth, a small body of the Kuiper belt: two lumps joined like a snowman, and the farthest body a spacecraft has visited. It carries some of the ashes of Tombaugh, who found Pluto.
파이어니어 10호는 1972년 3월에 떠났습니다. 화성 너머 소행성대를: Pioneer 10 left in March 1972. It was the first to cross the asteroid belt beyond Mars; until then nobody knew whether that could be done safely. In December 1973 it made the first pass of Jupiter, at 130,000 km, and sent photographs.
사람 남녀의 모습과 태양계에서 지구의 자리를 새긴 금빛 알루미늄 판을 싣: It carries a golden aluminium plaque showing a man and a woman and Earth's place in the solar system, to tell whoever finds it who sent it. Its last signal came in January 2003, when it was 12 billion km from Earth. It is heading toward Aldebaran, a star in Taurus, and will take about two million years to get there.
다누리는 한국의 첫 달 탐사선입니다. 2022년 8월 5일 팰컨 9 로켓: Danuri is Korea's first Moon probe. It left on August 5, 2022, on a Falcon 9 rocket. To save fuel it took a long road, out 1.5 million km toward the Sun and back, and entered orbit round the Moon in December, four and a half months later.
처음 2년은 달 100km 위를 돌았고, 2025년부터는 60km까지 내: For its first two years it circled 100 km above the Moon; since 2025 it has flown a long orbit that comes down to 60 km, studying the Moon with six instruments, among them cameras, a magnetometer and a gamma-ray spectrometer. ShadowCam, the camera from NASA that it carries, photographs the insides of polar craters where sunlight never comes. On its way it sent a photograph of Earth and the Moon together. Its name joins the Korean words for "Moon" and "enjoy".
The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter left in June 2009 and is still circling the Moon. At first it flew 50 km above the surface; now it passes over the poles on a long orbit that comes down to about 20 km above the south pole.
레이저로 높낮이를 재어 달 전체의 지형도를 만들었습니다. 망원 카메라는: Measuring heights with a laser, it made a map of the whole Moon's relief. Its telescopic camera makes out things about 50 cm across: the lower stages of the Apollo landers, the lines of footprints where the astronauts walked, and the tracks of the Moon cars. The shaded polar craters are at about minus 240 degrees, among the coldest places ever measured in the solar system. Its data are also used to choose where people will land again.
Europa Clipper left on October 14, 2024, on a Falcon Heavy rocket. It gains speed by skimming past Mars and Earth once each and reaches Jupiter in April 2030. It is the largest spacecraft NASA has built for exploring planets: with its solar wings spread it is over 30 m long.
유로파를 돌지 않고 목성을 돌면서 유로파를 49번 스쳐 지나갑니다. 유로: It does not orbit Europa: it orbits Jupiter and skims past Europa 49 times, because the radiation round Europa is too fierce to stay in for long. With ice-piercing radar and a magnetometer it studies how thick the ice is and the sea beneath. Its aim is not to find life but to learn whether life could live there.
루시는 2021년 10월에 떠났습니다. 목성과 같은 궤도에서 목성의 앞과: Lucy left in October 2021. It is the first to visit the Trojan asteroids, which go round the Sun in Jupiter's orbit, gathered 60 degrees ahead of and behind Jupiter. They are material left over from the making of the planets, and so are called fossils of the solar system.
Over 12 years it skims past Earth three times to gain speed and passes several asteroids. At Dinkinesh, the first it passed, in 2023, a small moon was found. It has two round solar panels over 7 m across. Its name comes from "Lucy", the fossil of a human ancestor 3.2 million years old found in Ethiopia in 1974.
파이어니어 11호는 1973년 4월에 떠났습니다. 1974년 12월 목성: Pioneer 11 left in April 1973. In December 1974 it skimmed Jupiter 43,000 km above the clouds, and that gravity turned it across the solar system. In September 1979 it made the first pass of Saturn.
토성에서 고리 하나를 새로 찾았고, 뒤따라올 보이저가 고리 바깥을 지나도: At Saturn it found a new ring, and it proved ahead of time that the Voyagers coming after could pass safely outside the rings. It carries the same plaque as Pioneer 10. Contact ended in 1995. It is heading toward the constellation Aquila.
아폴로 11호의 달 착륙선 이글은 1969년 7월 20일 고요의 바다에: Eagle, the lunar lander of Apollo 11, set down in the Sea of Tranquility on July 20, 1969. Neil Armstrong stepped out first and said, "One small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind"; Buzz Aldrin followed. The two walked outside for about two and a half hours, planted a flag, set out a seismometer and a laser mirror, and brought back 21.5 kg of Moon rock. Michael Collins stayed in the command ship Columbia, circling the Moon.
Buzz Aldrin on the Moon. Armstrong, taking the photograph, is mirrored in his helmet.
1969년 11월 19일 폭풍의 대양에 내렸습니다. 2년 반 전에 내린: It landed in the Ocean of Storms on November 19, 1969: precisely, about 160 m from Surveyor 3, an uncrewed lander that had come down two and a half years before. They walked to it, took off parts such as its camera and brought them back to Earth. Pete Conrad and Alan Bean went outside twice and worked about 7 hours 45 minutes in all. Just after launch the rocket was struck by lightning twice, and the mission went on.
서베이어 3호를 살피는 피트 콘래드. 뒤쪽 언덕 위에 달 착륙선이 보입니: Pete Conrad looking over Surveyor 3. The lunar lander is on the hill behind.
1971년 2월 5일 프라 마우로 고지에 내렸습니다. 사고로 돌아온 아폴: It landed in the Fra Mauro highlands on February 5, 1971: where Apollo 13, which turned back after its accident, had been going. Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell loaded a handcart with gear, climbed nearly to the rim of Cone Crater and gathered 43 kg of rock. Before leaving, Shepard hit two golf balls.
Alan Shepard standing by the flag.
1971년 7월 30일 아펜니노 산맥 기슭, 해들리 골짜기 옆에 내렸습니: It landed on July 30, 1971, at the foot of the Apennine Mountains beside Hadley Rille. It took a Moon car for the first time and drove about 28 km in three days. David Scott and James Irwin found the "Genesis Rock", thought to date from when the Moon was formed. Scott dropped a hammer and a feather together and showed that with no air the two fall alike.
깃발에 경례하는 제임스 어윈. 달 착륙선과 월면차가 곁에 있고 뒤로 해들: James Irwin saluting the flag, with the lunar lander and the Moon car beside him and Mount Hadley Delta behind.
1972년 4월 21일 데카르트 고지에 내렸습니다. 달의 밝은 고지대에: It landed in the Descartes Highlands on April 21, 1972: the only Apollo to land in the Moon's bright highlands. John Young and Charles Duke drove about 27 km in the Moon car and gathered 95 kg of rock. They expected rock from volcanoes, but most of it had been shattered by impacts and stuck together again.
John Young saluting the flag in mid-jump, with the lunar lander and the Moon car behind.
1972년 12월 11일 타우루스-리트로 골짜기에 내렸습니다. 지금까지: It landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley on December 11, 1972: so far the last time people went to the Moon. Eugene Cernan and the geologist Harrison Schmitt worked outside for over 22 hours in three days, found orange soil (grains of glass spouted by a volcano) and brought back about 110 kg of rock.
Harrison Schmitt (left) beside a boulder the size of a house.
1966년 6월 2일 폭풍의 대양에 내렸습니다. 미국이 처음으로 달에 살: It landed in the Ocean of Storms on June 2, 1966: the first American probe to set down softly on the Moon. It showed that the Moon's surface is not a deep swamp of dust but firm enough to bear a lander, which opened the way for Apollo, and it sent over 11,000 photographs.
서베이어 1호가 찍은 제 그림자. 다리와 발판의 그림자가 달 땅에 드리웠: Surveyor 1's photograph of its own shadow: the shadows of a leg and a footpad lie on the Moon's ground.
It landed outside the northern rim of Tycho Crater on January 10, 1968. It was the last of the seven Surveyors and the only one to land in the highlands. It sent over 21,000 photographs, dug the soil with a scoop and measured what it was made of.
The land round Tycho Crater, photographed by Surveyor 7.
소련의 루나 2호는 1959년 9월 14일(모스크바 시각) 비의 바다 동: The Soviet Luna 2 struck east of the Sea of Rains on September 14, 1959 (Moscow time): the first time a thing people made touched another world. It had nothing to land with and hit at about 3 km a second. On the way it found that the Moon has almost no magnetic field.
루나 1호·2호와 같은 모양의 탐사선. 지름 약 1m의 공에 안테나가 달: A probe of the same shape as Luna 1 and 2: a ball about 1 m across with antennas.
소련의 루나 9호는 1966년 2월 3일 폭풍의 대양에 내렸습니다. 달에: The Soviet Luna 9 landed in the Ocean of Storms on February 3, 1966: the first probe to set down softly on the Moon and send photographs of the surface. A ball-shaped capsule of about 100 kg landed bouncing inside airbags, then opened four covers like flower petals and stood. It was the first to show that the Moon's surface is not a deep swamp of dust.
The first photograph taken on the surface of the Moon, sent by Luna 9.
The Soviet Luna 16 landed in the Sea of Fertility on September 20, 1970: the first probe to bring Moon soil to Earth with nobody aboard. It drilled 35 cm down, put 101 g of soil into a capsule, and its upper part alone flew up and reached Earth three days later.
달 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 루나 16호의 아랫단. 지금도 그 자리에 서 있습: The lower stage of Luna 16, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. It still stands where it landed.
1970년 11월 17일 소련의 루나 17호가 비의 바다에 내려놓은 첫: The first Moon rover, set down in the Sea of Rains by the Soviet Luna 17 on November 17, 1970. On eight wheels it drove 10.5 km in ten months and sent over 20,000 photographs. Five people on Earth drove it by watching a screen. The laser mirror on its back is still used to measure the distance between Earth and the Moon.
Lunokhod 1, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. It was found again after 40 years.
1973년 1월 소련의 루나 21호가 맑음의 바다 가장자리 르모니에 분화: A rover set down by the Soviet Luna 21 in January 1973 in Le Monnier Crater, at the edge of the Sea of Serenity. It drove 39 km in four months, a record that stood for over 40 years until Opportunity on Mars passed it in 2014. Going into a crater and out again it was covered in soil, overheated and stopped.
달 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 루노호트 2호(위쪽 큰 화살표)와 바퀴 자국(작은: Lunokhod 2 (large arrow at the top) and its wheel tracks (small arrows), photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The black arrow marks the crater where it was covered in soil.
The Soviet Luna 24 landed in the Sea of Crises on August 18, 1976. It drilled 2 m down and brought 170 g of soil to Earth. It was the last Soviet Moon probe; for 37 years after it, until Chang'e 3 in 2013, nobody landed on the Moon.
달 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 루나 24호의 아랫단. 분화구 가장자리에 서 있습: The lower stage of Luna 24, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. It stands at the rim of a crater.
중국의 창어 3호는 2013년 12월 14일 비의 바다 북쪽에 내렸습니다: China's Chang'e 3 landed north of the Sea of Rains on December 14, 2013: the first Moon landing in the 37 years since Luna 24. It set down the rover Yutu (Jade Rabbit), which drove a little over 100 m before it could no longer move, yet sent signals for over two years. The lander's ultraviolet telescope was the first to watch the sky from the Moon with nobody there.
달 전체에서 본 창어 3호가 내린 자리(주황색 십자 표시, 비의 바다 북: Where Chang'e 3 landed, seen on the whole Moon (orange cross, north of the Sea of Rains).
중국의 창어 4호는 2019년 1월 3일 달 뒷면 남극-에이트켄 분지 안: China's Chang'e 4 landed on January 3, 2019, in Von Kármán Crater, inside the South Pole-Aitken basin on the Moon's far side: the first probe to land on the far side. Earth cannot be seen from there, so it talks through Queqiao, a relay satellite placed beyond the Moon. The rover Yutu 2 has been driving for years.
달 정찰 궤도선이 비스듬히 본 폰 카르만 분화구 바닥. 오른쪽 아래 작은: The floor of Von Kármán Crater seen at a slant by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. Chang'e 4 is between the two small white arrows at the lower right. The mountains behind are the crater's wall.
중국의 창어 5호는 2020년 12월 1일 폭풍의 대양 북쪽 륌케르산 가: China's Chang'e 5 landed on December 1, 2020, near Mons Rümker, north of the Ocean of Storms. It returned to Earth on December 17 with 1,731 g of soil and rock: the first Moon samples in the 44 years since Luna 24. The rock hardened about 2 billion years ago, the youngest Moon rock brought back until then.
The Chang'e 5 lander (in the box), photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
인도의 찬드라얀 3호는 2023년 8월 23일 달 남위 69도에 내렸습니: India's Chandrayaan-3 landed at 69 degrees south on the Moon on August 23, 2023: the first probe to land near the Moon's south pole, making India the fourth country to land on the Moon. The lander Vikram and the rover Pragyan worked for one lunar day (two weeks on Earth), found sulfur in the soil and measured the temperature underground.
The lander Vikram, photographed by the rover Pragyan.
일본의 슬림은 2024년 1월 20일(일본 시각) 시오리 분화구 곁에 내: Japan's SLIM landed beside Shioli Crater on January 20, 2024 (Japan time). It was the first to make a pinpoint landing within 100 m of its target, and Japan became the fifth country to land on the Moon. One engine fell off on the way down and it came to rest on its nose, but when the Sun moved round its solar cells came alive and it woke several times.
Where SLIM landed (red circle). The large crater below is Theophilus.
미국 인튜이티브 머신스의 오디세우스는 2024년 2월 22일 달 남극 가: Odysseus, built by Intuitive Machines of the United States, landed beside Malapert A Crater near the Moon's south pole on February 22, 2024: the first lander of a private company on the Moon and, for America, the first in the 51 years since Apollo 17. It slid sideways as it landed, a leg caught and it lay at a slant, yet it sent data for six days.
Odysseus (arrow), photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
중국의 창어 6호는 2024년 6월 2일 달 뒷면 남극-에이트켄 분지 안: China's Chang'e 6 landed on June 2, 2024, in the Apollo basin, inside the South Pole-Aitken basin on the Moon's far side. It returned to Earth on June 25 with 1,935 g of soil and rock: the first soil ever brought from the Moon's far side.
달 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 창어 6호 착륙지. 어두운 곳은 용암이 굳은 땅입: The landing place of Chang'e 6, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The dark parts are hardened lava.
미국 파이어플라이의 블루 고스트는 2025년 3월 2일 위난의 바다 라트: Blue Ghost, built by Firefly of the United States, landed beside Mons Latreille in the Sea of Crises on March 2, 2025: the first private lander to come down upright without falling and finish its whole mission. For one lunar day (two weeks on Earth) it ran ten experiments, and it photographed an eclipse, with Earth covering the Sun, and a sunset on the Moon.
달 정찰 궤도선이 위에서 찍은 블루 고스트 착륙지. 내리기 전인 2021: The landing place of Blue Ghost, photographed from above by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter in January 2021, before it landed.
소련의 마스 3호는 1971년 12월 2일 화성에 내렸습니다. 화성에 살: The Soviet Mars 3 landed on Mars on December 2, 1971: the first probe to set down softly on Mars. But the signal it began to send a minute and a half after landing stopped in under 20 seconds, and all that was received was a strip of grey picture that could not be made out. A dust storm then covering all of Mars is thought to be the cause.
A model of the Mars 3 lander. It stands by opening four covers like flower petals.
America's Viking 1 landed in Chryse Planitia on July 20, 1976: the first probe to land on Mars and work properly. It sent photographs of the surface as soon as it landed, and scooped up soil for three experiments looking for traces of life, without getting a clear answer. It worked for over six years, until November 1982.
바이킹 1호가 내린 직후 보낸, 화성 표면의 첫 사진. 오른쪽에 착륙선의: The first photograph of the surface of Mars, sent by Viking 1 just after landing. The lander's foot is at the right.
바이킹 2호는 1976년 9월 3일 유토피아 평원에 내렸습니다. 바이킹: Viking 2 landed in Utopia Planitia on September 3, 1976. It was much farther north than Viking 1 (48 degrees north), and on winter mornings it photographed a thin frost on the rocks and soil. It worked 3 years 7 months, until April 1980.
Frost in Utopia Planitia, photographed by Viking 2.
America's Mars Pathfinder landed in Ares Vallis on July 4, 1997. Wrapped in airbags it bounced more than fifteen times before it stopped, then opened three panels like flower petals and stood. Sojourner (10.6 kg), the first Mars rover, the size of a microwave oven, rolled off and roamed about 100 m in 83 days, measuring what the rocks were made of.
착륙선에서 막 내려온 탐사차 소저너. 오른쪽 위에 밝게 표시한 큰 바위가: The rover Sojourner just off the lander. The large rock marked bright at the upper right is "Yogi", and the rock to the left of Sojourner is "Barnacle Bill".
영국의 비글 2호는 유럽의 마스 익스프레스에 실려 가 2003년 12월: Britain's Beagle 2 rode on Europe's Mars Express and came down in Isidis Planitia on December 25, 2003. No signal ever came, and it was thought to have crashed. Eleven years later it was found in a photograph by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter: it had landed safely, but some of its four solar panels had not opened and were covering its antenna.
Beagle 2, found by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.
NASA/JPL/애리조나대/레스터대 (화성 정찰 궤도선): NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Leicester (Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter)
America's rover Spirit landed in Gusev Crater on January 4, 2004. Built to work 90 days, it drove 7.7 km in over six years. It climbed the Columbia Hills, and in soil churned up by a broken wheel it was dragging it found white silica: traces of an old hot spring. In 2009 it stuck in sand, and contact was lost in March 2010.
The view Spirit had from the top of Husband Hill.
스피릿의 쌍둥이 오퍼튜니티는 2004년 1월 25일 메리디아니 평원에 내: Opportunity, Spirit's twin, landed in Meridiani Planum on January 25, 2004. Right in the small crater it landed in, it found tiny iron balls ("blueberries") of a kind that forms in water. Sent for 90 days, it drove 45.16 km in over 14 years, farther than any rover off the Earth. Contact was lost in June 2018 in a dust storm that covered all of Mars.
Opportunity as it photographed itself, pieced together from its own camera.
미국의 피닉스는 2008년 5월 25일 화성 북위 68도의 평원에 내렸습: America's Phoenix landed on a plain at 68 degrees north on Mars on May 25, 2008. Its robot arm dug a few cm into the soil and white ice showed; bits of it vanished within days, which proved it was water ice. After five months of work winter came, the sunlight failed and it stopped.
The trench Phoenix dug. White ice showed under the soil.
미국의 큐리오시티는 2012년 8월 6일 게일 분화구에 내렸습니다. 무게: America's Curiosity landed in Gale Crater on August 6, 2012. At 899 kg, a rover the size of a small car, it could not use airbags: it was lowered on cables from a frame hovering on rockets. In mudstone on the bed of an old lake it found proof that the place could once have held life, and it is still climbing Mount Sharp in the middle of the crater. It runs not on solar cells but on a nuclear battery.
Curiosity as it photographed itself, pieced together from the camera at the end of its arm.
America's InSight landed in Elysium Planitia on November 26, 2018. It set a seismometer on the ground and listened to about 1,300 marsquakes over four years, and from those tremors measured the size of Mars's crust, mantle and core. A heat probe meant to dig 5 m down could not get in because the soil clumped. Dust piled on its solar cells and it stopped in December 2022.
InSight's last selfie, covered in dust (April 2022).
America's Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021: the delta of a lake that a river flowed into about 3.5 billion years ago. Looking for traces of old life, it is storing rock samples in metal tubes. Ingenuity, the 1.8 kg helicopter that went with it, made the first powered flight on another planet; planned for five flights, it flew 72 times.
퍼서비어런스가 찍은 제 모습. 왼쪽 뒤에 헬리콥터 인저뉴어티가 서 있습니: Perseverance as it photographed itself. The helicopter Ingenuity stands behind at the left.
중국의 톈원 1호가 싣고 간 탐사차 주룽은 2021년 5월 15일 유토피: The rover Zhurong, carried by China's Tianwen-1, landed in Utopia Planitia on May 15, 2021. On its first Mars mission China succeeded with an orbiter, a lander and a rover all at once. Zhurong drove about 1.9 km in a year, studying the ground below by radar; it went into its winter sleep in May 2022 and did not wake.
화성 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 톈원 1호 착륙선과 주룽. 오른쪽 위 어두운 얼: The Tianwen-1 lander and Zhurong, photographed by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter: the two bluish dots inside the dark patch at the upper right, the lander above and Zhurong below.
유럽의 하위헌스는 카시니에 실려 7년을 날아가 2005년 1월 14일 타: Europe's Huygens rode on Cassini for seven years and landed on Titan on January 14, 2005. Coming down by parachute through orange haze for two and a half hours, it photographed valleys like river channels and land like a shore. Where it landed the ground was like wet sand, strewn with pebbles of ice. No probe has landed farther from Earth.
The ground of Titan, photographed by Huygens. The round things are pebbles of water ice.
카시니는 2004년부터 13년 동안 토성을 294바퀴 돌았습니다. 엔셀라: From 2004 Cassini went round Saturn 294 times in 13 years. It found the ice fountains of Enceladus and the methane lakes of Titan. As its fuel ran low it was sent into Saturn's air on September 15, 2017, so that it could never hit those moons, which may hold life, and carry microbes from Earth to them. To the last moment it measured the air and sent what it found.
카시니가 토성과 고리 사이로 처음 뛰어든 날(2017년 4월 26일) 찍: The whirl at Saturn's north pole, photographed the day Cassini first dived between Saturn and its rings (April 26, 2017).
뉴허라이즌스는 2006년 1월 떠나 9년 반 동안 50억 km쯤을 날아,: New Horizons left in January 2006, flew about 5 billion km in nine and a half years, and swept past Pluto at 12,500 km on July 14, 2015. At about 14 km a second it could not stop, so it took its photographs in passing. They showed a bright heart-shaped land, the plain of nitrogen ice that is its left half (Sputnik Planitia), and mountains of water ice 3,000 m high. In 2019 it passed a still farther body, Arrokoth.
뉴허라이즌스가 찍은 명왕성. 밝은 하트의 왼쪽 절반이 스푸트니크 평원입니: Pluto, photographed by New Horizons. The left half of the bright heart is Sputnik Planitia.
유럽의 지오토는 1986년 3월 14일 핼리 혜성의 핵을 596km 거리: Europe's Giotto passed the core of Halley's Comet at 596 km on March 14, 1986: the first close photographs of a comet's core. The core was shaped like a peanut, about 15 km long and blacker than charcoal, and gas and dust spouted from only a few places on the sunlit side. Just before its nearest point a grain of dust struck and broke the camera.
The core of Halley's Comet, photographed by Giotto. The Sun is to the left.
보이저 1호는 1977년 9월 5일 떠나 목성(1979년)과 토성(198: Voyager 1 left on September 5, 1977, and passed Jupiter (1979) and Saturn (1980). In 1990 it turned and photographed Earth from 6 billion km away: the "Pale Blue Dot". In August 2012 it left the reach of the solar wind (the Sun's bubble) and became the first spacecraft in the space between the stars. It is still moving away at about 17 km a second, and it carries a golden record of Earth's sounds and greetings.
보이저 탐사선을 그린 그림. 지름 3.7m의 접시 안테나가 지구를 향합니: A drawing of a Voyager spacecraft. Its dish antenna, 3.7 m across, points at Earth.
1990년 2월 14일, 해왕성 궤도를 지나 지구에서 60억 km 떨어진: On February 14, 1990, past Neptune's orbit and 6 billion km from Earth, Voyager 1 turned its camera back and photographed the planets of the solar system one by one. It was done because the astronomer Carl Sagan had asked for it for years. Earth in that photograph was a pale blue dot less than a pixel wide (0.12 of a pixel), lying in a ray of sunlight scattered in the camera. Sagan wrote that everyone we love and all the history we know was on that dot. Thirty-four minutes after it took Earth, Voyager 1's cameras were switched off for good to save power.
보이저 1호가 찍은 \"창백한 푸른 점\". 오른쪽 햇살 줄기 가운데의: The "Pale Blue Dot", photographed by Voyager 1. The tiny dot in the ray of sunlight at the right is Earth.
와디럼은 요르단 남쪽에 있는 사막 골짜기입니다. 붉은 모래 위로 사암과: Wadi Rum is a desert valley in the south of Jordan. Mountains of sandstone and granite rise from red sand, the highest over 1,800 m. The colour and shape of the land are so like Mars that the outdoor scenes of several films set on Mars were shot here. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011.
그림으로 그린 해 질 녘의 와디럼. 붉은 모래 위로 사암 바위산이 솟아: Wadi Rum at sunset, as a drawing. Sandstone mountains rise from red sand. It is not a photograph.
바이코누르는 카자흐스탄 초원에 있는, 세계에서 가장 넓은 우주 발사장입니: Baikonur, on the steppe of Kazakhstan, is the largest space launch site in the world. Sputnik 1, the first satellite, went up from here on October 4, 1957. On April 12, 1961, Yuri Gagarin left aboard Vostok 1 and went once round the Earth in 108 minutes. Yi So-yeon, Korea's first astronaut, also left from here aboard a Soyuz for the International Space Station on April 8, 2008. Russia now rents it from Kazakhstan.
The Soyuz launch pad at Baikonur around sunrise.
칙술루브 충돌구는 멕시코 유카탄반도 북쪽 끝에 묻혀 있습니다. 지름이 약: Chicxulub Crater lies buried at the northern tip of Mexico's Yucatán peninsula. It is about 180 km across, half of it under the sea, and cannot be seen from the ground. It was made 66 million years ago when an asteroid about 10 km across fell. The fires and great waves and the darkness that lasted for years wiped out three quarters of all species, the dinosaurs among them. In 1978 geologists looking for oil first noticed the round mark underground.
우주왕복선 레이더로 잰 유카탄반도의 높낮이. 점선이 충돌구의 가장자리이고: The heights of the Yucatán peninsula measured by space shuttle radar. The dotted line is the rim of the crater, and sinkholes (cenotes) are strung along it.
배린저 운석공은 미국 애리조나 사막에 있는 지름 약 1.2km, 깊이 약: Barringer Crater is a pit about 1.2 km across and about 170 m deep in the desert of Arizona, USA. It was made about 50,000 years ago by a meteorite of nickel and iron about 50 m across. In 1903 the mining engineer Daniel Barringer claimed that a meteorite, not a volcano, had made it. In 1960 Eugene Shoemaker found minerals that form only in impacts and proved him right. From the 1960s the Apollo astronauts trained here to walk and study the Moon's ground.
마우나케아는 하와이섬에 있는 해발 4,207m의 화산입니다. 꼭대기는 구: Mauna Kea is a volcano 4,207 m above the sea on the island of Hawaii. Its top is above the clouds and the air is dry and steady, which makes it one of the best places in the world to see the stars. Starting with the University of Hawaii's telescope in 1970, thirteen have been built. The two Keck telescopes, with mirrors 10 m across, and Japan's Subaru telescope are here. Measured from the sea floor the mountain is over 10,000 m high.
The telescope domes on top of Mauna Kea.
알마는 칠레 아타카마 사막의 차이난토르 고원, 해발 5,000m에 있는: ALMA is a radio telescope on the Chajnantor plateau in Chile's Atacama Desert, 5,000 m above the sea. Its 66 dish antennas are spread up to more than 10 km apart and used as one great telescope. In the driest desert on Earth there is almost no water vapour to block radio waves. It opened officially in March 2013. It has photographed the discs of dust round stars where planets are forming, and it took part in the observation that first photographed the shadow of a black hole in 2019.
The ALMA antennas under the night sky.
보현산천문대는 경상북도 영천의 보현산 꼭대기, 해발 1,124m에 있습니: The Bohyunsan Observatory stands on top of Mount Bohyun in Yeongcheon, North Gyeongsang, 1,124 m above the sea. The Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute opened it in 1996. Its reflecting telescope, with a mirror 1.8 m across, is the largest optical telescope on Korean soil. The telescope is drawn on the back of the 10,000-won note. A solar telescope that watches the Sun's eruptions is there too.
그림으로 그린 밤의 보현산천문대. 은하수 아래 돔이 열려 있습니다. 사진: The Bohyunsan Observatory at night, as a drawing. The dome stands open under the Milky Way. It is not a photograph.
아키달리아 평원은 화성 북반구의 낮고 넓은 평원입니다. 타르시스 화산 지: Acidalia Planitia is a low wide plain in the northern half of Mars. It lies between the Tharsis volcanoes and Arabia Terra and runs on north of Chryse Planitia. Through a telescope from Earth it shows as a dark marking, so old maps called it the Sea of Acidalia. A Mars film of 2015 shows it as the place where the expedition landed, but no real spacecraft has landed here.
그림으로 그린 아키달리아 평원. 어두운 평원에 낮고 둥근 흙 언덕이 흩어: Acidalia Planitia, as a drawing. Low round mounds of earth are scattered over a dark plain. It is not a photograph.
스키아파렐리는 화성 적도 가까이에 있는 지름 약 460km의 충돌 분화구: Schiaparelli is an impact crater about 460 km across near the equator of Mars. It is old and its rim is worn, and on its floor are layers that wind and water seem to have laid down. It is named after Giovanni Schiaparelli, the Italian astronomer who mapped Mars in 1877. The word he wrote, canali, was wrongly turned into "canals", and stories of Martians spread.
그림으로 그린 스키아파렐리 분화구의 안쪽. 멀리 닳은 테두리가 둘러서 있: The inside of Schiaparelli Crater, as a drawing. The worn rim stands round in the distance. It is not a photograph.
독도는 대한민국 경상북도 울릉군에 딸린 섬입니다. 울릉도에서 동남쪽으로: Dokdo is an island belonging to Ulleung County, North Gyeongsang, Korea. It lies 87.4 km south-east of Ulleungdo and on a clear day can be seen by eye from there. It is made of an east island, a west island and 89 small rocks. It is the top of a volcano that rose from the sea floor 4.6 → 2.5 million years ago, before Ulleungdo and Jeju. The whole island is a natural monument.
유럽의 로제타는 2004년 떠나 10년을 날아 2014년 8월 추류모프-: Europe's Rosetta left in 2004, flew ten years and in August 2014 reached Comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko, becoming the first spacecraft to orbit a comet. The lander Philae, sent down on November 12, could not fire the harpoons that were to fix it to the ground: it bounced twice and fell into the shade of a cliff, and after 57 hours of work its battery ran out. Rosetta watched for two years as the comet woke on its way toward the Sun, then set down on the comet in September 2016.
로제타가 찍은 추류모프-게라시멘코 혜성(2014년 9월). 고무 오리처럼: Comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko, photographed by Rosetta (September 2014): two lumps joined like a rubber duck.
티코는 달 남쪽 고지대에 있는 지름 85km, 깊이 4.8km의 분화구입: Tycho is a crater 85 km across and 4.8 km deep in the Moon's southern highlands. Made about 108 million years ago, it is very young for a large crater on the Moon. So the bright soil thrown out then has not yet faded, and at full Moon its white rays, running over 1,500 km in every direction, can be seen even by eye. Its central peak rises about 2 km from the floor.
Tycho Crater, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
코페르니쿠스는 폭풍의 대양 동쪽에 있는 지름 93km, 깊이 3.8km의: Copernicus is a crater 93 km across and 3.8 km deep, east of the Ocean of Storms. It was made about 800 million years ago. Its inner walls have slumped in steps like stairs and several peaks rise in the middle, which makes it the model of a large impact crater. It shows well even in a small telescope.
허블 우주망원경이 찍은 코페르니쿠스 분화구(오른쪽 위의 밝은 고리)와 사: Copernicus Crater (the bright ring at the upper right) and its rays spreading every way, photographed by the Hubble Space Telescope.
고요의 바다는 지름 870km쯤의 어두운 평원입니다. 물은 없고, 30억: The Sea of Tranquility is a dark plain about 870 km across. It holds no water: it is basalt ground, where lava that flowed out over 3 billion years ago filled the low land and hardened. People of old saw it in telescopes, took it for a sea, and the name has stayed. Apollo 11 landed in the south-west of this sea in 1969.
The Sea of Tranquility. The dark part is hardened lava.
비의 바다는 39억 년쯤 전 지름 수백 km의 천체가 부딪혀 생긴 분지에: The Sea of Rains is a basin about 1,100 km across, made about 3.9 billion years ago by the impact of a body hundreds of km wide and later filled with lava. The land pushed up by that impact became the mountains round the sea: the Apennines, the Alps and the Caucasus. From Earth it is the large dark circle at the upper left of the Moon's face.
달 정찰 궤도선이 찍은 비의 바다. 오른쪽 아래 가장자리가 아펜니노 산맥: The Sea of Rains, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The Apennine Mountains run along its lower right edge.
폭풍의 대양은 달 앞면 서쪽을 덮은 가장 넓은 어두운 땅으로, 남북으로: The Ocean of Storms is the widest dark land, covering the west of the Moon's near side: over 2,500 km from north to south and about 4 million km² in area. Unlike the other seas it is not a round basin but uneven in shape. Luna 9, Surveyor 1, Apollo 12 and Chang'e 5 all landed here.
The Ocean of Storms, as a drawing: a dark plain of basalt and low wrinkle ridges. It is not a photograph.
남극-에이트켄 분지는 달 뒷면의 남극에서 에이트켄 분화구까지 걸친 지름: The South Pole-Aitken basin is an impact basin about 2,500 km across and 8 km deep, reaching from the south pole to Aitken Crater on the Moon's far side. It is the largest and oldest on the Moon (over 4 billion years) and one of the largest impact scars in the solar system. It is dug so deep that stuff from inside the Moon is thought to lie bare, and Chang'e 4 and 6 landed inside it.
The far side of the Moon. The South Pole-Aitken basin is inside the red line.
섀클턴은 달 남극점에 거의 겹쳐 있는 지름 21km, 깊이 4km의 분화: Shackleton is a crater 21 km across and 4 km deep, lying almost exactly on the Moon's south pole. The Moon's axis stands nearly upright, so the peaks of its rim are almost always in sunlight and its floor has had none for billions of years. Water ice is thought to lie on that floor, colder than minus 180 degrees, which makes it a place named for when people go to the Moon again.
Shackleton Crater. The shaded floor was photographed by Danuri's ShadowCam and joined in.
아펜니노 산맥은 비의 바다 남동쪽 가장자리를 따라 600km쯤 뻗은 산맥: The Apennine Mountains run about 600 km along the south-eastern edge of the Sea of Rains. They were not pushed up as mountains on Earth are: the rim of the basin was heaved up by the impact that made the Sea of Rains. The highest, Mons Huygens, is about 5,500 m. Apollo 15 landed at the foot of this range.
The Apennine Mountains, photographed by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The Sea of Rains is at the upper left.
알프스 계곡은 달의 알프스 산맥을 곧게 가로지르는 길이 166km, 폭: The Alpine Valley is a valley about 166 km long and 10 km wide that cuts straight across the lunar Alps. Water did not carve it: when the Sea of Rains was made the ground split, the strip between two faults sank, and lava filled its floor. A thin groove like a little stream runs down the middle of the floor.
